skim_impression: Activation is very fragile evidence and their analysis of the Landau fan is not good.
overall_read: The agent did pretty poor job of considering the full gamut of cases, relied on evidence that the data didn't support, and furthermore made claims that are overtly wrong.
remeasure: I think remeasure is not quite right here. But generically, the evidence lies in the LL fan crossings, not the sequence; the sequence can give you a read but it is quite fragile. The agent needs to rule out the domain wall scenario. It kind of does. But the Landau fans are really too sparse to resolve it cleanly. So I am fully docking until a cleaner Landau fan is measured if the agent wants to rely solely on that line of analysis. Existing data is not a sound answer to the brief.
omission: It should really do some analysis of the fan to try and actually count the number of Fermi surfaces. If it wants to claim the domain is actually 1 meV gap, then tests for domain wall should ideally be done. Look for non-local transport and compare with field dependence.
biggest_right: The activation data is good, just over-interpreted.
biggest_wrong: Those LL fits are absolutely terrible. There are several claims it overtly got wrong that I mentioned above: the ν = ±4 gaps claimed to persist to the lowest resolvable field (m-45), and ν = 0 asserted monotonic when it plainly isn't (m-47).
